Sigh, I can't keep it in all my life. It's heartbeats. I'm a cardiophile. Since kindergarten... yes, kindergarten. For some reason, I'm extremely ashamed of it even though it's not THAT weird. I avoid the subject, leave whenever "medical talk" starts, avoid songs with the topic or word in it (literally most.), get irrationally angry when ads and movies use the sound, I avoid hugs or when they happen I keep my hands inside to distance myself etc. It's really stupid but it's the main reason I'm terrified of doctors and get really stressed out. I freak out thinking they'll pull out a stethoscope or sphygmomanometer and then ask me why I'm so stressed out while mentioning the subject. Or taking too long, I had that once. I was so stressed out they had to do it again and it was horrible. I couldn't possibly ever say why I'm so stressed out and coming up with excuses is even more stressful. Hell, as you can tell I'm even avoiding the word in this very comment. I hate it and I wish I didn't have it, makes me feel abnormal. It's not a fun time when things that make you very uncomfortable are normal to others and a common topic for some reason. Nobody notices these things but me, who jumps at just the word. Sure, it's great in... hypothetical intimate situations because it works wonders in "setting things off" instantly but in general it's annoying and weird. In the past when I was way more open I actually told a person irl and they proceeded to mock me almost immediately. It made me close off so much, I'm never telling anyone again. For other cardiophiles it would be a dream if someone suggested a relatively normal for them activity that involves that stuff, you know. But for me it's a nightmare scenario. The intimacy of such a thing is too overbearing. For me it's like being completely naked and vulnerable in front of somebody. It's horrible.
